LIB-GMR-001.title: Distributed Cooperation
LIB-GMR-001.principle: Core cooperative stages should distribute essential information, access, or timing across multiple players so success comes from combining actions, not from one player directing everyone else.
LIB-GMR-001.implementation: When generating a cooperative stage, give different players different pieces of the solution. One player might see a symbol, another might hear a sound cue, another might reach a physical sensor, and another might control timing. Start with information-splitting, then add physical separation or simultaneous triggers when the stage needs stronger cooperation. Use time pressure carefully, mainly for advanced or high-energy stages. The stage should still allow players to communicate, coordinate, and feel shared success rather than simply obeying one dominant player.
LIB-GMR-001.rationale: This prevents the alpha-player problem while supporting real group cohesion. Players are not just standing near each other; they each hold something the group needs. This creates participation, communication, trust, and replayable variation without requiring new hardware for every stage.
LIB-GMR-001.aiRule: Before finalizing a cooperative stage, check whether one player can complete it alone by holding all information, reaching all sensors, and controlling all timing. If yes, split one required element across players: information first, physical access second, timing pressure third. Ensure the split creates meaningful cooperation, not just artificial inconvenience.

LIB-GMR-002.title: Fail Forward
LIB-GMR-002.principle: A failed objective should redirect the story, never dead-end it. Every failure state must hand players a new, playable situation â€” a harder path, a consequence, or a lead â€” so momentum and morale survive setbacks.
LIB-GMR-002.implementation: For each stage, author the failure branch as deliberately as the success branch. A failed puzzle might trigger an alarm that reroutes enemies, spend a resource, or unlock a slower manual bypass. Avoid outcomes that force players to stand idle or leave the game. Prefer consequences that change the board (new enemy behaviour, a locked route, a time penalty) over consequences that simply say "no".
LIB-GMR-002.rationale: Real-life games cannot pause and retry cleanly; a hard dead-end strands players physically and kills a session. Fail-forward design keeps everyone in motion, turns mistakes into story, and lets weaker teams still reach an ending.
LIB-GMR-002.aiRule: For every stage with a fail state, verify a defined next action exists on failure. If failure leads to "nothing happens" or "wait and try again", replace it with a consequence that changes the game state or opens an alternate route before finalizing.

LIB-GMR-003.title: Safety Breaks Fiction
LIB-GMR-003.principle: Player safety and consent always override the fiction. Any real-world hazard, medical need, or a player invoking a stop signal immediately pauses the in-game situation, no matter how dramatic the moment.
LIB-GMR-003.implementation: Every stage must define a safe-word / stop-signal response and a nearest out-of-game safe zone. Physical challenges declare their real limits (no grappling, no stairs, no blindfold near hazards) up front. Crew are briefed that enforcing safety is never "breaking immersion" â€” it is part of the job. Mark exits, hazards and med locations on the location map.
LIB-GMR-003.rationale: A single injury or ignored consent breach ends trust in the whole event. Encoding safety as a first-class rule keeps the game repeatable, insurable, and welcoming to new and vulnerable players.
LIB-GMR-003.aiRule: Before finalizing any stage involving physical action, restricted senses, or time pressure, confirm it names a stop-signal behaviour and a safe zone. If either is missing, add it and flag the stage for a crew safety review.

APM-ACTION-POINTS.label: Action Points
APM-ACTION-POINTS.description: Players receive a limited action budget and spend it on available actions.
APM-ACTION-POINTS.coreRule: Players receive a limited action budget and spend it on available actions.

APM-ACTION-DRAFTING.label: Action Drafting
APM-ACTION-DRAFTING.description: Players choose limited actions from a shared pool, making those choices unavailable to others.
APM-ACTION-DRAFTING.coreRule: Players choose limited actions from a shared pool, making those choices unavailable to others.

APM-ACTION-RETRIEVAL.label: Action Retrieval
APM-ACTION-RETRIEVAL.description: Used actions become unavailable until a player retrieves or refreshes them.
APM-ACTION-RETRIEVAL.coreRule: Used actions become unavailable until a player retrieves or refreshes them.

APM-ACTION-EVENT.label: Action / Event
APM-ACTION-EVENT.description: A player chooses between using an action resource and resolving a special event.
APM-ACTION-EVENT.coreRule: A player chooses between using an action resource and resolving a special event.

APM-COMMAND-CARDS.label: Command Cards
APM-COMMAND-CARDS.description: Cards determine which units, roles, or participants may act.
APM-COMMAND-CARDS.coreRule: Cards determine which units, roles, or participants may act.

APM-ACTION-QUEUE.label: Action Queue
APM-ACTION-QUEUE.description: Players program actions that resolve later in a defined sequence.
APM-ACTION-QUEUE.coreRule: Players program actions that resolve later in a defined sequence.

APM-SHARED-ACTION-QUEUE.label: Shared Action Queue
APM-SHARED-ACTION-QUEUE.description: Players contribute to one common queue whose actions affect everyone.
APM-SHARED-ACTION-QUEUE.coreRule: Players contribute to one common queue whose actions affect everyone.

APM-FOLLOW.label: Follow
APM-FOLLOW.description: One participant selects an action and others may perform the same or a modified version.
APM-FOLLOW.coreRule: One participant selects an action and others may perform the same or a modified version.

APM-ORDER-COUNTERS.label: Order Counters
APM-ORDER-COUNTERS.description: Players commit hidden or visible orders to locations before resolving them.
APM-ORDER-COUNTERS.coreRule: Players commit hidden or visible orders to locations before resolving them.

APM-RONDEL.label: Rondel
APM-RONDEL.description: Available actions follow a circular sequence, with movement determining access or cost.
APM-RONDEL.coreRule: Available actions follow a circular sequence, with movement determining access or cost.

APM-ACTION-SELECTION-RESTRICTIONS.label: Action Selection Restrictions
APM-ACTION-SELECTION-RESTRICTIONS.description: Rules restrict which actions a participant may currently choose.
APM-ACTION-SELECTION-RESTRICTIONS.coreRule: Rules restrict which actions a participant may currently choose.

APM-VARIABLE-PLAYER-POWERS.label: Variable Player Powers
APM-VARIABLE-PLAYER-POWERS.description: Different players or teams receive unique actions or modifications to shared actions.
APM-VARIABLE-PLAYER-POWERS.coreRule: Different players or teams receive unique actions or modifications to shared actions.

APM-ONCE-PER-GAME-ABILITIES.label: Once-per-Game Abilities
APM-ONCE-PER-GAME-ABILITIES.description: A powerful special action may be used only once during the game.
APM-ONCE-PER-GAME-ABILITIES.coreRule: A powerful special action may be used only once during the game.

APM-ADVANTAGE-TOKEN.label: Advantage Token
APM-ADVANTAGE-TOKEN.description: A transferable token grants or modifies a special action for its current holder.
APM-ADVANTAGE-TOKEN.coreRule: A transferable token grants or modifies a special action for its current holder.

APM-GATING-AND-UNLOCKING.label: Gating and Unlocking
APM-GATING-AND-UNLOCKING.description: Actions become available only after a condition, threshold, stage, or discovery.
APM-GATING-AND-UNLOCKING.coreRule: Actions become available only after a condition, threshold, stage, or discovery.

APM-TECH-TREES-TRACKS.label: Tech Trees / Tracks
APM-TECH-TREES-TRACKS.description: Progress unlocks new actions or improves actions already available.
APM-TECH-TREES-TRACKS.coreRule: Progress unlocks new actions or improves actions already available.

APM-EVENTS.label: Events
APM-EVENTS.description: An external event immediately changes the game state or later actions.
APM-EVENTS.coreRule: An external event immediately changes the game state or later actions.

APM-NARRATIVE-CHOICE.label: Narrative Choice
APM-NARRATIVE-CHOICE.description: Players choose between actions presented through a narrative situation.
APM-NARRATIVE-CHOICE.coreRule: Players choose between actions presented through a narrative situation.

APM-BINGO.label: Bingo
APM-BINGO.description: Randomly presented elements determine which actions or patterns players pursue.
APM-BINGO.coreRule: Randomly presented elements determine which actions or patterns players pursue.

APM-LAYERING.label: Layering
APM-LAYERING.description: Overlapping physical components determine which visible areas or actions are active.
APM-LAYERING.coreRule: Overlapping physical components determine which visible areas or actions are active.

APM-SLIDE-PUSH.label: Slide / Push
APM-SLIDE-PUSH.description: Moving one object pushes or repositions other objects in its path.
APM-SLIDE-PUSH.coreRule: Moving one object pushes or repositions other objects in its path.

APM-MATCHING.label: Matching
APM-MATCHING.description: A new action or component must match a visible feature of an earlier one.
APM-MATCHING.coreRule: A new action or component must match a visible feature of an earlier one.

APM-DRAWING.label: Drawing
APM-DRAWING.description: A participant represents something visually for others to interpret or guess.
APM-DRAWING.coreRule: A participant represents something visually for others to interpret or guess.

APR-HIGH-NUMBER.label: High Number
APR-HIGH-NUMBER.description: Compare generated totals; the highest qualifying result wins or succeeds.

APR-CRITICAL-HITS-AND-FAILURES.label: Critical Hits and Failures
APR-CRITICAL-HITS-AND-FAILURES.description: Extreme results create unusually strong successes or unusually costly failures.

APR-RATIO-COMBAT-RESULTS-TABLE.label: Ratio/Combat Results Table
APR-RATIO-COMBAT-RESULTS-TABLE.description: Compare opposing strengths as a ratio, then read the resulting outcome from a table.

APR-DIE-ICONS.label: Die Icons
APR-DIE-ICONS.description: Resolve the attempt by counting or interpreting symbols rather than ordinary die totals.

APR-CARD-PLAY.label: Card Play
APR-CARD-PLAY.description: Players commit or reveal cards whose values and effects determine the result.

APR-ROCK-PAPER-SCISSORS.label: Rock, Paper, Scissors
APR-ROCK-PAPER-SCISSORS.description: Simultaneous choices resolve through a circular pattern of strengths and weaknesses.

APR-PRISONER-S-DILEMMA.label: Prisoner's Dilemma
APR-PRISONER-S-DILEMMA.description: Each participant chooses whether to cooperate or defect, with the combined choices shaping the payoff.

APR-ALTERNATE-REMOVAL.label: Alternate Removal
APR-ALTERNATE-REMOVAL.description: Participants alternately remove available options until the remaining state determines the outcome.

APR-PHYSICAL-ACTION.label: Physical Action
APR-PHYSICAL-ACTION.description: Real-world accuracy, speed, coordination, or dexterity directly determines the result.

APR-STATIC-CAPTURE.label: Static Capture
APR-STATIC-CAPTURE.description: A fixed spatial relationship determines whether an area, target, or piece is captured.

APR-ENCLOSURE.label: Enclosure
APR-ENCLOSURE.description: An outcome is achieved by surrounding or enclosing a target, region, or opposing element.

APR-MINIMAP.label: Minimap
APR-MINIMAP.description: A smaller representation of the play space is used to resolve position, movement, or control.

APR-FORCE-COMMITMENT.label: Force Commitment
APR-FORCE-COMMITMENT.description: Players secretly or openly allocate limited strength before comparing commitments.

APR-VOTING.label: Voting
APR-VOTING.description: Participants collectively determine an outcome by casting and counting preferences.

APR-PLAYER-JUDGE.label: Player Judge
APR-PLAYER-JUDGE.description: A player evaluates an answer, performance, or interpretation and decides the result.

APR-TARGETED-CLUES.label: Targeted Clues
APR-TARGETED-CLUES.description: Specific information is directed to selected participants to shape deduction and resolution.

APR-TIEBREAKERS.label: Tiebreakers
APR-TIEBREAKERS.description: A secondary comparison or rule determines the result when the primary method is tied.

APR-DICE-SELECTION.label: Dice Selection
APR-DICE-SELECTION.description: Players choose which dice to roll, keep, use, or assign before resolving the result.

APR-ACTION-SPEED.label: Action Speed
APR-ACTION-SPEED.description: The order or speed with which actions are completed determines priority or success.

APR-REROLLING-AND-LOCKING.label: Rerolling and Locking
APR-REROLLING-AND-LOCKING.description: Players preserve selected results while rerolling others to improve or complete an outcome.

APR-KILL-STEAL.label: Kill Steal
APR-KILL-STEAL.description: Credit or reward goes to the participant who completes the decisive final contribution.

APR-HOT-POTATO.label: Hot Potato
APR-HOT-POTATO.description: A risky state or object passes between participants until a timer or trigger resolves it.

APR-FLICKING.label: Flicking
APR-FLICKING.description: Players propel components with a finger flick, using the resulting position or contact as the outcome.

APR-STACKING-AND-BALANCING.label: Stacking and Balancing
APR-STACKING-AND-BALANCING.description: Players build or balance physical components, with stability and placement determining success.

APR-NEIGHBOR-SCOPE.label: Neighbor Scope
APR-NEIGHBOR-SCOPE.description: Resolution affects or compares only adjacent participants, spaces, or elements.

VC-VICTORY-POINTS-FROM-GAME-STATE.label: Victory Points from Game State
VC-VICTORY-POINTS-FROM-GAME-STATE.description: Award victory points for reaching or maintaining defined states in the game.

VC-VICTORY-POINTS-FROM-PLAYER-ACTIONS.label: Victory Points from Player Actions
VC-VICTORY-POINTS-FROM-PLAYER-ACTIONS.description: Award victory points directly for specific actions completed by players.

VC-TEMPORARY-AND-PERMANENT-VICTORY-POINT.label: Temporary and Permanent Victory Points
VC-TEMPORARY-AND-PERMANENT-VICTORY-POINT.description: Distinguish points that can still be lost from points secured permanently.

VC-VICTORY-POINTS-AS-A-RESOURCE.label: Victory Points as a Resource
VC-VICTORY-POINTS-AS-A-RESOURCE.description: Let players spend, exchange, or otherwise use victory points during play.

VC-HIDDEN-AND-EXPOSED-VICTORY-POINT.label: Hidden and Exposed Victory Point
VC-HIDDEN-AND-EXPOSED-VICTORY-POINT.description: Mix concealed victory-point information with scores that remain visible to everyone.

VC-ENDGAME-BONUSES.label: Endgame Bonuses
VC-ENDGAME-BONUSES.description: Award additional victory points when final conditions are evaluated at the end of play.

VC-RACE.label: Race
VC-RACE.description: The first player or team to reach a defined destination or objective wins.

VC-PLAYER-ELIMINATION.label: Player Elimination
VC-PLAYER-ELIMINATION.description: Players leave contention as elimination conditions are met until a winner remains.

VC-FIXED-NUMBER-OF-ROUNDS.label: Fixed Number of Rounds
VC-FIXED-NUMBER-OF-ROUNDS.description: End the game after a predetermined number of rounds and evaluate the winner.

VC-EXHAUSTING-RESOURCES.label: Exhausting Resources
VC-EXHAUSTING-RESOURCES.description: End or resolve the game when a defined supply, deck, or other resource is depleted.

VC-COMPLETING-TARGETS.label: Completing Targets
VC-COMPLETING-TARGETS.description: Win by completing a required set or number of objectives.

VC-FIXED-NUMBER-OF-EVENTS.label: Fixed Number of Events
VC-FIXED-NUMBER-OF-EVENTS.description: End the game after a predetermined number of events have occurred.

VC-ELAPSED-REAL-TIME.label: Elapsed Real Time
VC-ELAPSED-REAL-TIME.description: Use a real-world time limit to determine when play ends or victory is checked.

VC-CONNECTIONS.label: Connections
VC-CONNECTIONS.description: Win by creating a required network, route, chain, or connection between objectives.

VC-CIRCUIT-BREAKER-SUDDEN-DEATH.label: Circuit Breaker, Sudden Death
VC-CIRCUIT-BREAKER-SUDDEN-DEATH.description: Trigger an immediate ending when a decisive condition or threshold is reached.

VC-FINALE.label: Finale
VC-FINALE.description: Resolve victory through a dedicated concluding phase after the main game.

VC-KING-OF-HILL.label: King of Hill
VC-KING-OF-HILL.description: Win by taking and holding control of a key position or objective.

VC-CATCH-THE-LEADER.label: Catch the Leader
VC-CATCH-THE-LEADER.description: Create victory pressure around reaching, stopping, or overtaking the current leader.

VC-TUG-OF-WAR.label: Tug of War
VC-TUG-OF-WAR.description: Move a shared advantage back and forth until one side reaches its winning threshold.

VC-HIGHEST-LOWEST.label: Highest Lowest
VC-HIGHEST-LOWEST.description: Determine victory by comparing the highest or lowest qualifying value at the end.

VC-ORDERING.label: Ordering
VC-ORDERING.description: Determine victory by achieving or predicting a required order of players, objects, or events.

UNC-BETTING-AND-BLUFFING.label: Betting and Bluffing
UNC-BETTING-AND-BLUFFING.description: Let players stake resources while concealing, exaggerating, or misrepresenting the strength of their position.

UNC-PUSH-YOUR-LUCK.label: Push Your Luck
UNC-PUSH-YOUR-LUCK.description: Let players choose between securing current gains and risking them for a greater reward.

UNC-MEMORY.label: Memory
UNC-MEMORY.description: Require participants to remember previously revealed information, positions, or sequences.

UNC-HIDDEN-ROLES.label: Hidden Roles
UNC-HIDDEN-ROLES.description: Assign concealed identities or responsibilities that shape player goals and behavior.

UNC-ROLES-WITH-ASYMMETRIC-INFORMATION.label: Roles with Asymmetric Information
UNC-ROLES-WITH-ASYMMETRIC-INFORMATION.description: Give different roles access to different information relevant to shared or competing decisions.

UNC-COMMUNICATION-LIMITS.label: Communication Limits
UNC-COMMUNICATION-LIMITS.description: Restrict what, when, or how participants may communicate information.

UNC-UNKNOWN-INFORMATION.label: Unknown Information
UNC-UNKNOWN-INFORMATION.description: Keep information unavailable to every participant until it is discovered or generated.

UNC-HIDDEN-INFORMATION.label: Hidden Information
UNC-HIDDEN-INFORMATION.description: Allow some participants to know information that remains concealed from others.

UNC-PROBABILITY-MANAGEMENT.label: Probability Management
UNC-PROBABILITY-MANAGEMENT.description: Let players influence, evaluate, or reduce uncertainty in random outcomes.

UNC-VARIABLE-SETUP.label: Variable Setup
UNC-VARIABLE-SETUP.description: Change starting conditions, resources, positions, or objectives between plays.

UNC-HIDDEN-CONTROL.label: Hidden Control
UNC-HIDDEN-CONTROL.description: Conceal which participant controls an element, area, or decision.

UNC-DEDUCTION.label: Deduction
UNC-DEDUCTION.description: Infer a specific hidden answer by combining evidence and eliminating possibilities.

UNC-INDUCTION.label: Induction
UNC-INDUCTION.description: Form a broader rule or pattern from several observed examples or clues.

UNC-QUESTIONS-AND-ANSWERS.label: Questions and Answers
UNC-QUESTIONS-AND-ANSWERS.description: Reveal or test information through structured questions and responses.

ECON-EXCHANGING.label: Exchanging
ECON-EXCHANGING.description: Allow players to exchange resources according to a defined rate or rule.

ECON-TRADING.label: Trading
ECON-TRADING.description: Allow players to negotiate and transfer resources directly between participants.

ECON-MARKET.label: Market
ECON-MARKET.description: Use a shared buying and selling space whose supply, demand, or prices can change.

ECON-DELAYED-PURCHASE.label: Delayed Purchase
ECON-DELAYED-PURCHASE.description: Separate payment from delivery so a purchase becomes available later.

ECON-INCOME.label: Income
ECON-INCOME.description: Provide recurring resources when a defined phase, interval, or condition occurs.

ECON-AUTOMATIC-RESOURCE-GROWTH.label: Automatic Resource Growth
ECON-AUTOMATIC-RESOURCE-GROWTH.description: Increase an owned resource automatically over time or between rounds.

ECON-LOANS.label: Loans
ECON-LOANS.description: Provide resources now in exchange for repayment, interest, or a future obligation.

ECON-ALWAYS-AVAILABLE-PURCHASES.label: Always Available Purchases
ECON-ALWAYS-AVAILABLE-PURCHASES.description: Keep selected purchases continuously available instead of limiting them to a changing market.

ECON-I-CUT-YOU-YOU-CHOOSE.label: I Cut You, You Choose
ECON-I-CUT-YOU-YOU-CHOOSE.description: One participant divides available value while another chooses which portion to take.

ECON-DISCOUNTS.label: Discounts
ECON-DISCOUNTS.description: Reduce a cost when a player meets a particular condition or possesses an advantage.

ECON-UPGRADES.label: Upgrades
ECON-UPGRADES.description: Spend resources to improve the value, efficiency, or capability of something already owned.

ECON-RANDOM-PRODUCTION.label: Random Production
ECON-RANDOM-PRODUCTION.description: Determine the amount or type of produced resources through a random process.

ECON-INVESTMENT.label: Investment
ECON-INVESTMENT.description: Commit resources now for a possible larger return later.

ECON-OWNERSHIP.label: Ownership
ECON-OWNERSHIP.description: Assign control or rights over resources, locations, actions, or other game elements.

ECON-CONTRACT.label: Contract
ECON-CONTRACT.description: Create an agreement that exchanges commitments, resources, or future actions.

ECON-BRIBERY.label: Bribery
ECON-BRIBERY.description: Offer resources or favors to influence another participant, role, or decision.

ECON-INCREASE-VALUE-OF-UNCHOSEN-RESOURCE.label: Increase Value of Unchosen Resources
ECON-INCREASE-VALUE-OF-UNCHOSEN-RESOURCE.description: Raise the future value of options that players leave unselected.

ECON-NEGOTIATION.label: Negotiation
ECON-NEGOTIATION.description: Let participants determine an exchange or agreement through direct discussion.

ECON-ALLIANCES.label: Alliances
ECON-ALLIANCES.description: Allow participants to coordinate resources or goals through temporary or lasting cooperation.

ECON-RESOURCE-QUEUE.label: Resource Queue
ECON-RESOURCE-QUEUE.description: Place resources or purchases in an ordered queue that controls when they become available.

AUC-OPEN-AUCTION.label: Open Auction
AUC-OPEN-AUCTION.description: Participants openly raise or change their bids while everyone can see the current offer.

AUC-ENGLISH-AUCTION.label: English Auction
AUC-ENGLISH-AUCTION.description: Bids increase openly until no participant is willing to exceed the highest bid.

AUC-TURN-ORDER-UNTIL-PASS-AUCTION.label: Turn Order Until Pass Auction
AUC-TURN-ORDER-UNTIL-PASS-AUCTION.description: Participants bid in turn and leave the auction when they pass.

AUC-SEALED-BID-AUCTION.label: Sealed Bid Auction
AUC-SEALED-BID-AUCTION.description: Participants submit hidden bids that are revealed and compared simultaneously.

AUC-SEALED-BID-WITH-CANCELLATION.label: Sealed Bid with Cancellation
AUC-SEALED-BID-WITH-CANCELLATION.description: Participants submit hidden bids with a rule that can cancel selected bids or the auction.

AUC-CONSTRAINED-BIDDING.label: Constrained Bidding
AUC-CONSTRAINED-BIDDING.description: Bids must follow defined limits, increments, resources, or eligibility requirements.

AUC-ONCE-AROUND-AUCTION.label: Once Around Auction
AUC-ONCE-AROUND-AUCTION.description: Each participant receives one opportunity to bid in a single pass around the group.

AUC-DUTCH-AUCTION.label: Dutch Auction
AUC-DUTCH-AUCTION.description: A price descends until a participant accepts the current offer.

AUC-SECOND-BID-AUCTION.label: Second Bid Auction
AUC-SECOND-BID-AUCTION.description: The highest bidder wins but pays the value of the second-highest qualifying bid.

AUC-SELECTION-ORDER-BID.label: Selection Order Bid
AUC-SELECTION-ORDER-BID.description: Bids determine the order in which participants choose rewards, actions, or positions.

AUC-MULTIPLE-LOT-AUCTION.label: Multiple Lot Auction
AUC-MULTIPLE-LOT-AUCTION.description: Several items or groups of items are auctioned within the same bidding process.

AUC-CLOSED-ECONOMY-AUCTION.label: Closed Economy Auction
AUC-CLOSED-ECONOMY-AUCTION.description: All bids and payments circulate within a limited game economy rather than leaving it.

AUC-REVERSE-AUCTION.label: Reverse Auction
AUC-REVERSE-AUCTION.description: Participants compete by offering progressively lower costs or requirements.

AUC-DEXTERITY-AUCTION.label: Dexterity Auction
AUC-DEXTERITY-AUCTION.description: Physical accuracy, speed, or coordination forms part of placing or resolving a bid.

AUC-FIXED-PLACEMENT-AUCTION.label: Fixed Placement Auction
AUC-FIXED-PLACEMENT-AUCTION.description: Participants place bids into fixed spaces whose positions affect the outcome.

AUC-DUTCH-PRIORITY-AUCTION.label: Dutch Priority Auction
AUC-DUTCH-PRIORITY-AUCTION.description: A descending offer determines both who accepts and the priority they receive.

AUC-BID-AS-WAGERS.label: Bid as Wagers
AUC-BID-AS-WAGERS.description: Bids act as stakes that can be won, lost, or resolved according to a later outcome.

AUC-AUCTION-COMPENSATION.label: Auction Compensation
AUC-AUCTION-COMPENSATION.description: Participants who lose or withdraw receive compensation based on their bids or position.

WP-STANDARD-WORKER-PLACEMENT.label: Standard Worker Placement
WP-STANDARD-WORKER-PLACEMENT.description: Place a limited worker on an available action space to perform or reserve that action.

WP-WORKERS-OF-DIFFERING-TYPES.label: Workers of Differing Types
WP-WORKERS-OF-DIFFERING-TYPES.description: Give different worker types distinct placement permissions, strengths, or effects.

WP-ACQUIRING-AND-LOSING-WORKERS.label: Acquiring and Losing Workers
WP-ACQUIRING-AND-LOSING-WORKERS.description: Allow the available worker pool to grow or shrink through game actions and consequences.

WP-WORKERS-AS-DICE.label: Workers as Dice
WP-WORKERS-AS-DICE.description: Use dice as workers so their rolled values affect where they can be placed or what they accomplish.

WP-ADDING-AND-BLOCKING-BUILDINGS.label: Adding and Blocking Buildings
WP-ADDING-AND-BLOCKING-BUILDINGS.description: Add action spaces through buildings while allowing placement or ownership to block access.

WP-SINGLE-WORKERS.label: Single Workers
WP-SINGLE-WORKERS.description: Limit an action space, area, or participant to one worker at a time.

WP-BUILDING-ACTIONS-AND-REWARDS.label: Building Actions and Rewards
WP-BUILDING-ACTIONS-AND-REWARDS.description: Connect worker placement on buildings to the actions and rewards those buildings provide.

WP-TURN-ORDER-AND-RESOLUTION-ORDER.label: Turn Order and Resolution Order
WP-TURN-ORDER-AND-RESOLUTION-ORDER.description: Use worker placement to establish turn priority or the order in which actions resolve.

MOV-TESSELLATION.label: Tessellation
MOV-TESSELLATION.description: Arrange repeating shapes so movement and adjacency follow the geometry of the play space.

MOV-ROLL-AND-MOVE.label: Roll and Move
MOV-ROLL-AND-MOVE.description: Roll a randomizer and move according to the resulting distance or instruction.

MOV-PATTERN-MOVEMENT.label: Pattern Movement
MOV-PATTERN-MOVEMENT.description: Move pieces according to a predefined spatial pattern.

MOV-MOVEMENT-POINTS.label: Movement Points
MOV-MOVEMENT-POINTS.description: Spend a limited allowance of points to move through spaces or terrain.

MOV-RESOURCE-TO-MOVE.label: Resource to Move
MOV-RESOURCE-TO-MOVE.description: Spend a resource in order to move or increase movement.

MOV-MEASUREMENT.label: Measurement
MOV-MEASUREMENT.description: Measure physical distance directly to determine legal movement.

MOV-DIFFERENT-DICE.label: Different Dice
MOV-DIFFERENT-DICE.description: Choose or assign different dice whose values and probabilities determine movement.

MOV-DRIFT.label: Drift
MOV-DRIFT.description: Apply automatic or persistent movement in a particular direction.

MOV-IMPULSE.label: Impulse
MOV-IMPULSE.description: Resolve movement in short shared steps or impulses rather than one complete move at a time.

MOV-PROGRAMMED-MOVEMENT.label: Programmed Movement
MOV-PROGRAMMED-MOVEMENT.description: Choose movement instructions in advance and reveal or execute them later.

MOV-RELATIVE-POSITION.label: Relative Position
MOV-RELATIVE-POSITION.description: Determine movement from the position or orientation of other pieces rather than a fixed map.

MOV-MANACLA.label: Manacla
MOV-MANACLA.description: Move groups of pieces by distributing them sequentially across spaces.

MOV-CHAINING.label: Chaining
MOV-CHAINING.description: Continue movement by linking one valid movement, space, or piece to the next.

MOV-BIAS.label: Bias
MOV-BIAS.description: Make movement more likely or effective in selected directions or conditions.

MOV-MOVING-MULTIPLE-UNITS.label: Moving Multiple Units
MOV-MOVING-MULTIPLE-UNITS.description: Move several units together, sequentially, or through one shared instruction.

MOV-MAP-ADDITION.label: Map Addition
MOV-MAP-ADDITION.description: Expand the available play space by adding new map areas during play.

MOV-MAP-PRODUCTION.label: Map reduction
MOV-MAP-PRODUCTION.description: Over the course of the game, the map shrinks

MOV-MAP-DEFORMATION.label: Map Deformation
MOV-MAP-DEFORMATION.description: Change the shape, connections, or accessibility of the existing map.

MOV-MOVE-THROUGH-DECK.label: Move Through Deck
MOV-MOVE-THROUGH-DECK.description: Represent movement by progressing through cards or an ordered deck.

MOV-MOVEMENT-TEMPO.label: Movement Template
MOV-MOVEMENT-TEMPO.description: A defined Movement Template is used to determine where a piece moves to.

MOV-PIECES-AS-MAP.label: Pieces as Map
MOV-PIECES-AS-MAP.description: Use placed pieces themselves to define spaces, routes, or terrain.

MOV-MULTIPLE-MAPS.label: Multiple Maps
MOV-MULTIPLE-MAPS.description: Use more than one connected or parallel play space for movement.

MOV-SHORTCUTS.label: Shortcuts
MOV-SHORTCUTS.description: Provide routes that reduce distance or bypass normal movement requirements.

MOV-HIDDEN-MOVEMENT.label: Hidden Movement
MOV-HIDDEN-MOVEMENT.description: Keep some or all movement information concealed from other participants.

AC-ABSOLUTE-CONTROL.label: Absolute Control
AC-ABSOLUTE-CONTROL.description: Control an area by meeting an exclusive requirement that prevents competing control.

AC-AREA-MAJORITY-INFLUENCE.label: Area Majority Influence
AC-AREA-MAJORITY-INFLUENCE.description: Control or score an area by having more influence there than competing participants.

AC-TROOP-TYPES.label: Troop Types
AC-TROOP-TYPES.description: Use units with different capabilities or values when establishing control over an area.

AC-TERRITORIES-AND-REGIONS.label: Territories and Regions
AC-TERRITORIES-AND-REGIONS.description: Organize the play space into defined areas that can be occupied, contested, or controlled.

AC-AREA-PERIMETERS.label: Area Perimeters
AC-AREA-PERIMETERS.description: Determine control through borders, enclosure, or presence around the edge of an area.

AC-FORCE-PROJECTION.label: Force Projection
AC-FORCE-PROJECTION.description: Extend influence or control from a unit, base, or nearby controlled area.

AC-ZONE-OF-CONTROL.label: Zone of Control
AC-ZONE-OF-CONTROL.description: Limit or affect movement and actions within the surrounding reach of a unit or position.

AC-LINE-OF-SIGHT.label: Line of Sight
AC-LINE-OF-SIGHT.description: Require an unobstructed visual or spatial path for influence, targeting, or control.

SET-SET-VALUATION.label: Set Valuation
SET-SET-VALUATION.description: Assign value according to the size, composition, rarity, or completeness of a collected set.

SET-TILE-LAYING.label: Tile Laying
SET-TILE-LAYING.description: Place tiles to create patterns, spaces, routes, or scoring relationships.

SET-GRID-COVERAGE.label: Grid Coverage
SET-GRID-COVERAGE.description: Score or progress by covering required cells, shapes, or regions of a grid.

SET-NETWORK-BUILDING.label: Network Building
SET-NETWORK-BUILDING.description: Connect elements into routes or networks that satisfy goals or generate value.

SET-COMBO-ABILITIES.label: Combo Abilities
SET-COMBO-ABILITIES.description: Combine collected elements so their abilities interact or produce a stronger effect.

CARD-TRICK-TAKING.label: Trick Taking
CARD-TRICK-TAKING.description: Participants play cards into tricks whose rules determine which card wins each exchange.

CARD-LADDER-CLIMBING.label: Ladder Climbing
CARD-LADDER-CLIMBING.description: Players successively play higher combinations until everyone else passes or cannot continue.

CARD-MELDING.label: Melding
CARD-MELDING.description: Combine cards into recognized sets or sequences to score, progress, or activate effects.

CARD-CARD-DRAW-LIMITS-AND-DECK-EXHAUSTIO.label: Card Draw Limits and Deck Exhaustion
CARD-CARD-DRAW-LIMITS-AND-DECK-EXHAUSTIO.description: Use limits on drawing and the depletion of a deck to control tempo, scarcity, or ending conditions.

CARD-DECK-BUILDING.label: Deck Building
CARD-DECK-BUILDING.description: Acquire cards during play to improve and specialize a personal deck.

CARD-DRAFTING.label: Drafting
CARD-DRAFTING.description: Choose cards from a shared or passing selection while leaving other choices for later participants.

CARD-DECK-CONSTRUCTION.label: Deck Construction
CARD-DECK-CONSTRUCTION.description: Build a deck before play according to defined composition and eligibility rules.

CARD-MULTI-USE-CARDS.label: Multi-Use Cards
CARD-MULTI-USE-CARDS.description: Allow each card to be used in more than one way, requiring a choice between its functions.

CARD-TAGS.label: Tags
CARD-TAGS.description: Use labels or traits on cards to create eligibility, combination, and interaction rules.
